checkpoint: 3 — the frame after, and the proof that the simulation did not notice
note: Same spec, same commands, same machine as evidence/77-scale-before.json; only the code between them differs. PNGs land under .artifacts/evidence/77-after/ and are not committed. Hashes and checksums are copied from the manifest capture-evidence.ps1 wrote (.artifacts/evidence/77-after/manifest.json).

after.commitSubject: Где рисуется тело — тоже проверяемо без движка (#77)

measuredBodySize.reportedBy: view.goblinWorldSize in each run's own godot_graybox_screenshot event
measuredBodySize.note: The engine reports the double the same expression produces; the last-place difference against 1360/22 is binary representation, which is why the test compares to 12 decimal places rather than bit-for-bit.

captures.name: 77-scale-rooms
captures.reading: The same crew on the same tick. Bodies fill their cells instead of sitting in the middle of them; face, tunic and the tool in hand are readable at 1x, which at 36.4 px they were not.

captures.name: 77-scale-raid
captures.reading: The crowding case the scale was chosen on. Fighters at the watch post now stand shoulder to shoulder, with the floor still visible between the rows — the 170-175 % behaviour the gate log describes, in the shipped renderer rather than in the spike scene.

captures.name: 77-scale-raid-detail
captures.reading: Byte-for-byte identical to its own «before» — and that is the point it makes. At 2x over this stretch of the map there is no body in frame, so the frame is walls, floor, room outlines, grid and HUD alone: none of them moved by a single pixel. The change is confined to bodies, measured rather than asserted.

simulationDidNotNotice.claim: Acceptance criterion 4 of Issue #77: the canonical checksum is the same before and after.
simulationDidNotNotice.method: Each capture's run publishes its own canonical checksum in the godot_graybox_screenshot event; capture-evidence.ps1 copies it into the manifest. The before and after manifests are compared field by field.
simulationDidNotNotice.whyItCouldNotHaveChanged: ADR 0011: DungeonFortress.Presentation reads the snapshot and writes nothing back, and it does not reference Godot; the constant added by this change lives there and is consumed only by drawing. The build itself is the guard — canonical state has no way to reach a number the renderer multiplies by.
simulationDidNotNotice.alsoCovered: The godot stage of scripts/verify.ps1 requires one checksum across camera position, zoom, frame size and UI scale, and the sim and load stages replay the command log and compare checksums. Both are in the full run recorded at checkpoint 5.

gridAndPivot.claim: Acceptance criterion 2: the grid, the cell size and the anchor a body is placed by did not change.
measured: CameraViewTests.Growing_the_body_moves_neither_the_grid_nor_the_point_a_body_is_placed_by: at tile 32, 40 and 48 the cell centre is still (x+0.5, y+0.5) tiles, WorldToCell round-trips it, WorldVisualScale is still tileSize/22, and CameraView.GoblinDrawRect is still centred on the render centre.
The 2x capture above: with no body in frame, the after PNG is byte-identical to the before PNG — walls, floor, outlines and grid are literally the same pixels.

whatDidMove.finding: A centred square grows in all four directions, so the drawn feet sink. Measured, not estimated: in all four v1 states the last opaque row is 92 of 96, so the feet are 92/96 of the way down the square — 16.67 px below the render centre before, 28.33 px after, a drop of 11.67 px, i.e. 29 % of a 40 px cell. Half a cell is 20 px, so the feet cross from inside the cell to just outside it.

theAlternative.correctedAfterReviewOfPR176: This entry first said that anchoring the square on the old foot line «holds the feet exactly still» and costs 2 Issue #156 crossings. Those are two different rules, and the sentence married the words of one to the measurement of the other. Independent review found the ~1 px discrepancy; both rules were then re-measured here from scratch before anything was rewritten.
theAlternative.command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .artifacts/anchors.ps1 for the geometry, and `dotnet test tests/DungeonFortress.Presentation.Tests/DungeonFortress.Presentation.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~No_stroke_above_the_depth_pass_lands_on_a_body_that_is_visible"` with CameraView.GoblinDrawRect temporarily set to each rule in turn, at tile 40 unless stated
theAlternative.sharedFacts: Body 36.363636 px before and 61.818182 px after; the v1 sheet's last opaque row is 92 of 96 in all four states, so the drawn feet are 92/96 of the way down the square and the remaining 4/96 is transparent padding that scales with it. Before the change the feet were 16.666667 px below the render centre.

ruleA_anchorTheDrawnFeet.whatItIs: Hold the drawn feet on the line they were on — the rule spike #142's own scene used (spikes/142-scale-spike/creature_visual.gd grows the body upward from a pivot at the feet).
ruleA_anchorTheDrawnFeet.reading: The feet really do not move, and this sweep finds nothing against it at any tile size.

ruleB_anchorTheSquaresBottomEdge.whatItIs: Hold the square's bottom edge where the old square's bottom edge was — the rule that was actually implemented and measured when this file was first written.
ruleB_anchorTheSquaresBottomEdge.feetMovementReading: negative: the feet RISE by 1.06 px, because the transparent 4/96 of padding under them grows with the square. So this rule does not hold the feet still either.
ruleB_anchorTheSquaresBottomEdge.crossingDetail: Both are the same body — mid-step between cells 21,6 and 21,7 — against the south edge of quarters@19,2 at cells 20,5 and 21,5. OverlapPx in the test payload is an AREA, width x height: 4.760331 and 0.495868 at tile 32, 7.438017 and 0.774793 at tile 40, 10.710744 and 1.115702 at tile 48. Spread over a body 61.8 px wide these are slivers, which is why rule A, only 1.06 px lower, clears them entirely.

theAlternative.whatThisChangesAboutTheFork: The reason recorded for not taking the upward rule — «it undoes part of Issue #156» — holds only for rule B. Rule A, the one that actually keeps the feet where the owner saw them in the spike, costs nothing this sweep can measure. The shipped behaviour is left as it is (a centred square) because that is what this change was reviewed on, but the fork now stands on different ground and is named as such in the handoff.

whatDidMove.notSettledHere: This change keeps the centred square and leaves the choice where the art that decides it lands: the next subtask of Issue #77 connects the v2 pack and must replace the square with a 17:12 rectangle (87.55 x 61.8 px), which is a placement decision in its own right. Raised in the handoff rather than settled quietly.
